description: WEBSITE DESIGN Customized websites built specifically for your goals. Your website is the face of your company online. It is the digital representation of your brand, your core values, your company vision, and most importantly it is your main marketing hub for your digital advertising strategy. As such, it is critical that you display the best possible version of your company to your customers via your website. Book a Strategy Call We Design Websites That Are... We Design Websites That Are... Responsive Responsive website designs are designs that are fluid, meaning that they are built to expand, contract, and resize images based on the browser we detect that is viewing the website. This is the preferred Google standard and we make sure you exceed the required expectations. Accessible Accessibility means your website is designed in such a way that users with disabilities can still consume your website content whether they are blind or colorblind. By adding specific tags that machines can read, your website will be able to be read even by the disabled. Fluid The fluid nature of responsive website design means that all users should get access to the same information regardless of the device they use to read it. Making sure that it responds fluidly to maximize each size of the browser is one of the areas that makes you an authority to search engines over your competitors. SEO Optimized One of the advantages of working with a full-service digital marketing agency on your new website design or website redesign is that we build it with SEO in mind. We make sure to implement all Google-recommended best practices for on-page SEO when we build your website! A carefully crafted digital portal that will be built for education, conversion, or any other strategy you may need. Created for conversions. Before we begin any website design project we determine what the primary objective is for your business. Do you prefer phone calls or form submissions? Do you want folks to chat live

title: A real team behind your results
description: Our Core Values Passion Care so much it doesn’t even make sense to anyone else. Passion and drive is everything in life. Be passionate about your work, for yourself and your company. We care about our company’s growth. We care about our individual growth. We care about the quality of our work. We care about growing our customer’s businesses Keeping passion in our daily lives requires consistency Kaizen Kaizen is a Japanese word that embodies continuous improvement of workplace and personal practices and efficiency. Always be looking for potential holes to be filled Always be looking for new ways to solve problems Always be looking for new ways to improve your own skills Always be looking for ways to improve our products and services The only way we can seek constant improvement is by taking pride in our work Teamwork Everything we do, we do it together. Because each one of our team members embodies our other core values of Passion, Consistency, Kaizen, and Pride, we are 100% confident in each other’s motivations, capabilities, and execution. Trust in team Deliver Together Consistency The key ingredient for success in anything is consistent effort. Consistency is about building small empowering habits and rituals that you partake in every single day to keep you focused on your highest priority goals. description:

1.) Creating a robust marketing campaign for your practice to maximize exposure to potential buyers. In today’s crowded + competitive sales environment, your clinic needs to have every possible advantage. We:

Because we have a very active sales cycle, as opposed to the passive model that most brokers employ, our team invests approximately 200 hours over the life of an average practice sale. The "white glove" service our team of 20+ provides resulted in industry breaking records in 2018:

- 50% shorter average sales cycle than the industry norm
- 98% completion from LOI to close
- 99.9% bank approval of loan applications submitted

title: Plumbing & Heating Business- Lakes Region, NH
description: File#: 226006 Price: $395,000 After 40 years of serving the Lakes Region, the owner of this established and profitable plumbing and heating business is ready to retire. He is prepared to stay on, as needed, to ensure a smooth transition for the right buyer. This is a turnkey opportunity with a loyal 600-member customer base, consistent annual sales exceeding $300,000, and average discretionary earnings of $150,000 per year. Ideal buyers include local or regional plumbing or HVAC companies looking to expand market share, journeyman plumbers ready to own their own business, construction companies needing reliable plumbing capacity, and home services businesses looking to broaden their offerings. Additionally, the 5,668 sq. ft. (.13 acre) property suitable for the businesses’ operation is available at a market value of $165,000. The property has a one vehicle heated garage on-site and is a buildable lot. title: What Buyers Really Want From a Business Sale
description: When you’re selling a business, it’s natural to focus on the number you want to receive. But experienced sellers know that a successful transaction involves much more than agreeing on a price. The amount of cash changing hands, the financing structure, the buyer’s ability to operate the business, and the expectations of both parties can all influence whether a deal actually comes together. The key is finding a structure that makes sense for both sides. A buyer may be willing to pay a strong price for a good business, but the amount of cash required upfront can have a significant impact on whether the transaction is workable. Seller financing can sometimes bridge that gap. Rather than requiring the buyer to provide the entire purchase price in cash at closing, a seller may finance a portion of the purchase. This can make the business accessible to a larger pool of qualified buyers while giving the seller the opportunity to receive payments over time. For buyers, the question is often simple: Can this business support the purchase price and provide enough income to make the investment worthwhile? For sellers, there’s a similar question: Can I structure the transaction in a way that gives the buyer a realistic chance to succeed while still achieving my financial goals? The best deal structure considers both. Qualified Buyers Matter Not every person who expresses interest in buying a business is ready or able to complete a transaction. A serious buyer should have a realistic understanding of the financial commitment involved, the responsibilities of ownership, and what it will take to operate the company successfully. This is one reason buyer qualification is such an important part of the selling process. A seller doesn’t simply need someone who likes the business. They need a buyer who has the financial resources, motivation, and ability to move forward. A qualified buyer also gives the seller greater confidence when considering terms such as seller financing. First Name Last Name Company Name Phone Email State Select State Alabama Alaska Arizona Arkansas California Colorado Connecticut Delaware Florida Georgia Hawaii Idaho Illinois Indiana Iowa Kansas Kentucky Louisiana Maine Maryland Massachusetts Michigan Minnesota Mississippi Missouri Montana Nebraska Nevada New Hampshire New Jersey New Mexico New York North Carolina North Dakota Ohio Oklahoma Oregon Pennsylvania Rhode Island South Carolina South Dakota Tennessee Texas Utah Vermont Virginia Washington West Virginia Wisconsin Wyoming Email Me the Questionnaire Get the Most for Your Firm The financial dictionary defines value as “ the worth of all rights arising from ownership of property. ” In the case of an accounting firm or a tax practice, most likely the largest asset that will be transferred in a sale will be the intangible portion of the business, or what we commonly refer to as goodwill. But sometimes valuing an intangible becomes an even bigger task. How do a seller and a buyer ever agree on the value of a firm? As a seller considers placing his or her business on the market, determining the most probable selling price (asking price) for the firm is very important. Too often the owner assigns an unrealistic or arbitrary value that leads to a lack of response from buyers and the loss of valuable time in the process. This can cause frustration to both the seller and interested buyers. At Accounting Biz Brokers, we know the market and can assist you in determining the most probable selling price for your business. title: Explore Business Listings for Sale in Colorado
description: OUR FOUNDER Christian Alavi Christian graduated from the University of Nebraska – Lincoln (Go Huskers!) majoring in Accounting and Finance and Masters of Professional Accountancy. Upon graduating he worked in a couple different roles at RSM McGladrey and Deloitte with their tax and audit teams. CONNECT WITH ME Having done audit and tax work from Fortune 500 companies to family owned companies on main street, he always knew his passion was small business. Working over 15 years with small businesses, Christian has a deep understanding of what it takes to succeed. He grew up in western SD within the family cattle ranch where he gained a passion for family owned companies.  His professional experience as a licensed CPA at RSM and Deloitte, has given him the experience and expert knowledge of companies’ tax compliance and financial statements. ​ After leaving Deloitte, he bought his first business (liquor store) and has continued to own, operate and consult with many family owned businesses. His diverse knowledge and experience combined with a genuine passion to help family owned companies succeed sets him apart. He firmly believes everyone should follow their passion and be involved in a family owned company. After all, it’s the fiber that holds us all together. Christian now lives in Red Cliff, CO with his beautiful daughter Karoline. His love for the outdoors include skiing, golfing, mountain biking and climbing among many many others the mountain life provides. He is still very active in the family cattle ranch and enjoys teaching his daughter the value of hard work and compassion for caring for animals.

description: Expertise You Can Trust At Van Daughtry Consulting, we pride ourselves on being experts in the business brokerage field. Our extensive experience and deep understanding of various industries make us the ideal partner for both buyers and sellers looking to navigate the complex world of business transactions. Book A Call Now Tailored Approach to Your Needs We understand that every business and individual is unique. Committed to Your Success Your success is our top priority. We’re committed to achieving the best possible outcome for you, whether that’s finding the perfect business to buy or securing the best price when selling your company. With our vast network and connections, we’re able to identify opportunities that others might miss. Specialty Markets Expertise At Van Daughtry Consulting, we understand that commercial real estate is an integral part of your business success. Our team of real estate professionals brings unparalleled expertise and local market knowledge to the table, ensuring you find the perfect property for your needs or get the best value for your commercial property when selling. Take the Next Step with Confidence Ready to embark on your business buying or selling journey? Trust Van Daughtry Consulting to provide the expertise, support, and personalized approach you need to navigate the process with confidence. Get in touch with us today and let’s discuss how we can help you achieve your goals. Book a Call

title: FHA Loan in Orange County – The Shortcut to Homeownership (Before It’s Too Late) | The DeBlis Group
description: FHA Loan in Orange County – The Shortcut to Homeownership (Before It’s Too Late) | The DeBlis Group Christian DeBlis Jan 8, 2025 4 min read FHA Loan in Orange County: Your Way In—Before the Market Moves Without You You’ve done everything right. You worked hard. You saved. You built your credit. And yet, owning a home in Orange County still feels out of reach. Prices climb. Competition gets fiercer. The market moves, and every month you’re stuck on the sidelines, watching as homes get snatched up by buyers who seem to have more—more cash, more connections, more of an inside track. Maybe you’ve told yourself, “Next year.” Maybe you think you need 20% down. Maybe you think your credit score isn’t good enough. Maybe you think waiting will help. It won’t. Here’s the truth: Most first-time buyers will wait too long. By the time they’re “ready,” the homes they could have afforded today will be out of reach. But the ones who win? They know something you don’t. They know about the FHA loan in Orange County. The FHA Loan in Orange County Is Your Shortcut—But Only If You Use It Right 3.5% down. That’s all you need. Not 20%. Not 10%. Three and a half percent. On a $700,000 home? That’s $24,500 down. On a $500,000 home? Just $17,500. That’s the difference between buying now and being locked out forever. And it’s not just about the down payment. Your credit score doesn’t have to be perfect. FHA loans allow scores as low as 580. Your debt won’t disqualify you. Car loans, student loans—FHA loans allow higher debt-to-income ratios. You don’t need endless savings. FHA lets you roll some closing costs into the loan. And here’s where it gets even better. An FHA loan in Orange County is assumable. That means if you buy now and lock in a low interest rate, you can sell later and pass that rate to the next buyer. In a rising-rate market? That’s gold. This isn’t just about owning a home today. It’s about controlling your future. What Happens If You Don’t Move Now? Let’s talk about waiting.

title: Sell A Business
description: Dr. Mark Hagar A lifelong resident of Fort Wayne, Indiana, Dr. Mark Hagar brings decades of hands-on experience in small business ownership, acquisitions, and turnarounds to his role as a business broker. Over his distinguished career, he has acquired and operated more than 20 companies and engineered over 50 successful turnarounds, giving him a uniquely practical understanding of what makes businesses succeed, and sell. His portfolio spans manufacturing, distribution, and service firms in industries including printing, education, military contracting, aerospace, and orthopedics. This diverse background enables him to identify value, anticipate buyer needs, and structure complex deals with confidence and precision. Mark holds a Doctorate in Business Administration (DBA) from Cranfield University’s School of Management in Bedford, England—one of Europe’s leading business schools. His research on small business resilience and operational excellence has been recognized by the Small Business Institute (SBI), the United States Association for Small Business and Entrepreneurship (USASBE), and the International Council for Small Business (ICSB). In addition to his business career, Dr. Hagar has served as a member of faculty at several institutions of higher education, including Holy Cross College (Notre Dame), Trine University, and the University of Saint Francis. He also hosted Your Business Matters, a small business–focused radio show and podcast for more than a decade and is the author of Small Fortunes – the Acquisition Entrepreneur’s Guide to Buying a Profitable Small Business. A passionate advocate for entrepreneurs, Mark previously chaired the Indiana Leadership Council for the National Federation of Independent Business (NFIB), representing small business owners before state and federal legislators. As your intermediary, we help control the release of information throughout the process so that you can run your daily operations and only have to engage with qualified buyers. title: Know What Your Practice Is Worth Before a Buyer Decides for You
description: Common questions What do I get? More than a number. You get a full valuation of your practice, the add-back analysis behind it, and a written plan: the specific things in your business putting value at risk today, and the improvements that will raise what buyers pay by the time you are ready to sell. What does it cost? A flat fee, covered in your booking call, and credited in full against our success fee if you sell with Platano Advisors within 12 months. Owners who go on to sell effectively pay nothing. They simply get their answers a year early. Will anyone know my practice is being valued? No. The assessment is confidential from start to finish. Your staff, your patients, and the market never know it happened. Many owners run it precisely because they want answers without signaling anything. What do you need from me? title: What Top Healthcare Dealmakers Expect in 2026, and What It Means for Medical Practice Owners
description: What Top Healthcare Dealmakers Expect in 2026, and What It Means for Medical Practice Owners Every year Axial asks the investors and advisors on its Healthcare Top 50 where the market is headed. Platano Advisors made the 2026 list , and the survey results are worth a close read if you own a medical practice. The short version: buyers are active, they are selective, and most deals that fail, fail over value. Here are the six findings that matter most to a seller, and what to do about each one. Source: Axial, 2026 Healthcare M&A Outlook Survey 1. Buyers want physician practices Physician practices ranked second for deal activity, named by 51.7% of surveyed dealmakers. Only behavioral health ranked higher, at 69.0%. What it means for you: demand is not the question. There are buyers for well-run medical practices right now, including strategic buyers and private equity groups building platforms. The real question is how many of them you get into a competitive process at the same time. That number, more than anything else, decides your price. 2. High activity does not mean a high multiple Here is the finding most owners do not expect. Physician practices ranked second for activity, yet they drew the largest share of “lower multiple” responses, at 30.8%. The same survey showed wide disagreement inside the category, with some dealmakers seeing strong valuations and others seeing weak ones. What it means for you: buyers are paying for specific practices, not for the specialty. The spread comes from factors you can see and, in many cases, change: how much revenue depends on you personally, how clean and documented your books are, your payer mix, and whether your staff and providers will stay. We cover how buyers sort practices in Two Numbers Decide What Your Practice Sells For . 3. title: Questions Business Owners Ask Before Selling
description: 1. Business Sale Planning & Readiness When is the right time to sell my business? The best time to sell is when your business is performing well, not when you’re burned out or desperate. Ideally, you want to sell when revenues are growing or stable, your financials are clean and well-documented, and market conditions favor sellers. In healthcare specifically, we’re seeing strong buyer demand right now driven by consolidation trends and a deep pool of active buyers — from strategic acquirers and independent sponsors to family offices, search funds, and private equity firms. What are common reasons owners at my size decide to sell? For small to mid-size healthcare businesses, the most common reasons are burnout and lifestyle change (especially post-COVID), approaching retirement with no succession plan, a desire to capitalize on strong market valuations, partnership disputes, and the increasing burden of regulatory compliance. description: COMMON QUESTIONS Your questions, answered directly. If something is unclear after reading through these, the next step is a conversation. We want to understand where your practice is before recommending anything. START A CONVERSATION Do I have to take everything, or can I start with one piece? You start with either the website or the CRM. Deal management is its own software, tied to the CRM, so it arrives with the CRM rather than being a separate starting point. Whichever you begin with is built to connect to the rest, so adding the next piece later is an extension rather than a rebuild. Who designs and builds the website? The Deal Studio design team. We work through who you serve, what you want to be known for, and how you talk about it, and the site gets built from what comes out of it. Its job is a website that says something specific about you from the day it launches rather than something generic. We work well with your other professional advisors like lawyers and accountants. We’ve done many transactions and know how to handle the complexities of selling a business. During the process, you, as the seller, keep doing what you’re good at – running the business. Our job is to keep things confidential, find potential buyers, screen them, educate them about your business, negotiate the sale terms, and help manage emotions. Our substantial database of pre-qualified buyers can also help you sell the business faster and more easily. What am I required to do during the selling process? At first, we need info from you or someone who knows a lot about the company. This info will be used for marketing and sales. Later, it’s important for the owner to keep growing the business like they will own it for a long time. If the company’s finances get worse after it’s put up for sale, it won’t sell well. Everyone in the business should focus on meeting the company’s goals. How do you handle confidentiality? We know that if people find out that a company might be sold, it can impact customers, employees, competitors, lenders, suppliers, and investors and lower the company’s value. We make sure that anyone interested in buying a company signs a paper promising not to share any confidential information about the company they want to buy. title: What is a Confidential Information Memorandum (CIM)?
description: Frequently Asked Questions What is included in a CIM? A CIM typically includes an executive summary, detailed company history, description of products and services, market analysis, management team bios, operational overview, and three to five years of financial data, including Value Drivers and adjusted EBITDA calculations. How does a CIM tell my company's story? A CIM tells your story by framing historical data within a narrative of future potential. It explains not just what the company has done, but why it is positioned for Growth Opportunities and how a new owner can leverage its existing strengths to achieve Financial Synergies. Who receives the CIM? The CIM is sent to qualified strategic and financial buyers who have signed a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) and demonstrated the financial capacity to complete the acquisition. This often includes competitors, private equity firms , and family offices. Does every business sale need a CIM? While very small "main street" businesses might use simpler profiles, any mid-market transaction requires a CIM. It is the professional standard that buyers expect and is necessary to drive a competitive bidding process. Preparing Your Business for the Market A confidential information memorandum is more than a document; it is the culmination of your life’s work as a business owner. It is the tool that transforms your operational reality into an investment opportunity. Because the CIM is often the first "deep look" a buyer gets at your company, its quality directly correlates to the quality of the offers you will receive. If you are considering an exit, the first step is understanding what your business is worth today. Whether you need a Compass Exit Opinion ™ to gauge the market or a full exit planning strategy , professional guidance ensures your CIM reflects the true value you’ve built. title: Discover the Market Value of Your Business: The Compass Exit Opinion™ Strategic Roadmap
description: Frequently Asked Questions What is my company worth? Your company's value is determined by a combination of financial metrics (like Adjusted EBITDA) and intangible assets (like brand reputation and management depth). The Compass Exit Opinion™ provides a market-based opinion of value based on current capital market conditions and recent transactions for companies with $10M–$250M in revenue. Is now the right time to sell my business? The right time to sell depends on both market cycles and your personal readiness. We analyze industry-specific trends, M&A market activity and comparable transaction data points, and your company's internal value drivers to help you determine if you should " Grow or Go ." If the market is favorable but your business has "detractors," we may suggest waiting until improvements are made. How do you sell a complex business like mine? Selling a complex business requires an elite M&A deal team that understands how to communicate your unique value proposition. We use the QuietAuction™ process to target sophisticated buyers who value your specific assets, your brand, and the team you have built, ensuring a smooth transition that protects your legacy. How much do I keep after the deal closes? The amount you keep depends on the M&A deal structure and tax planning. We perform a Net After-Tax Proceeds Analysis to help you understand the impact of taxes, liabilities, and transaction terms on your final cash-at-close. I received an unsolicited offer. Should I take it? Remember, one buyer is no buyer. An unsolicited offer can be a useful data point, but accepting one without preparation often leaves significant value on the table. Before responding, it is important to know your Adjusted EBITDA, your NWC position, and the current market range for your industry. title: Choosing An Intermediary

description: Choosing An Intermediary As a business owner, someday you will want to exit your business, preferably on your terms. When that time comes, how will you find and more importantly assess  a qualified professional to help you complete the sale? In general, a business  seller should look for a business intermediary who practices full-time in  facilitating the transfer of business ownership. A full-time intermediary  should know what it takes to value, list, confidentially market, and sell  businesses. To help you determine if we, or any other intermediary, are a good  match for you, start by asking a few basic questions such as: "Have you ever owned a business of your  own?" "How long have you been selling businesses?" "What  size transactions have you closed?" Most business intermediaries  will have prepared responses to such questions and they may give you some basic  information that will help you to determine the background and experience an  intermediary can bring to bear in selling your business. But as most of us are aware, responses to such questions may be those which we  want or expect to hear. These  responses shed little light as to how an intermediary will behave with you in  challenging and complex situations where personal motives and emotions can cloud  objectivity. To learn more, you may want  to investigate how the intermediary has dealt with challenging issues in the  past. Understanding the intermediary’s  actions and decisions in real life situations will give you a more in depth  sense of how they will represent your business and interests. description: The Premier Transaction™ NOTE:  The fundamental aspects of selling a business seem simple; value the business, market the business, negotiate offers from buyers and close the sale. However in reality, divestiture of your privately held business can be one of the most difficult challenges you as the owner will encounter. The decision surrounding divestiture of your business is a major event and is often the most important financial decision you will make. The stakes are high and the obstacles often varied and complex. Yet ironically, these issues are among those for which you the owner may have limited experience since you may only encounter them once in a lifetime. You may have decades of experience managing your business, but little or no experience with the important and often complex task surrounding your exit. Having an experienced team on your side with an effective and structured process is vital to exiting your business on your terms with maximum value. Exit Plan for Transfer to Key Insider(s) Business:  Manufacturer of Tech Component Parts At the time of engagement with Premier Sales, the company was being sought by a publicly traded company.  However, the company was business owner centric – meaning the company’s success and future revenue stream was too reliant upon the business owner.  Often, heavy reliance upon the owner results in a self-imposed ceiling on revenue. And, in this case, the gross revenue was too low and the reliance on the owner was too much for a publicly traded company to move forward with their interest.  In reality, a transfer of the business, in that condition, to any party would have resulted in onerous terms and conditions unacceptable to the owner. Together, we developed an Exit Plan and put it into action.  This involved identifying and on-boarding a key insider, developing an incentive plan with golden handcuffs and creates two exit strategies.  Through this process of developing a plan, the company and its team have a road map.

title: Financing The Business Acquisition
broker_name: premier sales, inc. diane t. thomas pllc, d.b.
description:
Financing The Business Acquisition Corporate downsizing in the U.S. has made owning a business a more attractive proposition than ever before.  As increasing numbers of prospective buyers embark on the process of becoming independent business owners, many of them voice a common concern: How do I finance the business acquisition? Prospective buyers are aware that tighter credit restrictions greatly prevent the traditional lending institution from being the likely solution to their needs. Where then, can buyers turn for help with what is likely to be the largest single investment of their lives? There are a variety of financing sources, and buyers can find one that fills their particular requirements. (Small businesses--those priced under $100,000 to $150,000--will usually depend on seller financing as the chief source.) For many businesses, the following are the best routes to follow: Buyer's Personal Equity In most business acquisition situations, this is the place to begin. Typically, anywhere from 20 to 50 percent of cash needed to purchase a business comes from the buyer and his or her family. Buyers should decide how much capital they are able to risk, and the actual amount will vary, of course, depending on the specific business and the terms of the sale. But, on average, a buyer should be prepared to come up with something between $25,000 and $150,000 for main street businesses.
One of the major reasons personal equity financing is a good starting point is that buyers who invest their own capital start the ball rolling--they are positively influencing other possible investors or lenders to participate. Seller Financing One of the simplest--and best--ways to finance the acquisition of a business is to work hand-in-hand with the seller. The seller’s willingness to participate will be influenced by his or her own risk tolerance, tax considerations, cash needs and comfort with the buyers ability to successfully operate the business. title: High-End Liquor Store with Real Estate
description: This is a rare opportunity to acquire a well-established, large-format liquor store together with the underlying real estate in a growing Colorado Front Range community. While overall sales moderated in 2026, the business improved profitability through a stronger product mix, disciplined expense management, and operational efficiencies. Operating successfully for more than 50 years, the store has built a loyal customer base, an excellent reputation, and a knowledgeable, experienced staff. Strategically located adjacent to a main highway, the property features an inviting, customer-focused layout, a broad selection of leading brands, and a carefully curated assortment of specialty products. The combined acquisition of the operating business and real estate presents an attractive opportunity for an industry buyer seeking expansion or a synergistic retailer looking to leverage the established customer base and further enhance profitability. Ownership is open to flexible transaction structures and terms, providing additional optionality for qualified buyers. DOWNLOAD BUSINESS SUMMARY

title: Market-Leading Heavy Infrastructure Contractor
description: For many decades, this civil construction contractor delivers utilities and structural concrete projects for federal and municipal clients across multiple states in the Rocky Mountain region. The company provides water, sewer, and storm infrastructure installation and rehabilitation and structural/civil concrete. The company is built on its established longterm client relationships and a strong reputation for executing complex projects on time and on budget, including federal contracts and large municipal programs. With a near $60M backlog for 2026 and annual revenue over $40M in the most recent fiscal year, upcoming projects are expected to support sustained annual revenue of $45M+ for years to come. The business has proven highly profitable, financially conservative, and supported by a modern technology platform covering accounting, estimating, equipment tracking, collaboration, and HR. Operations are scalable, with management ready to ensure a smooth transition. Growth opportunities include expanding alternative delivery contracts, executing additional municipal and federal projects, and disciplined market development within the company’s existing footprint. This represents a strategic acquisition opportunity for a partner seeking a stable, highperforming contractor with strong backlog, repeat clients, and proven execution. VIEW BUSINESS SUMMARY

title: Fully Equipped Sport Fishing Charter Operation
description: This well-established pier and fishing charter business offers an exceptional turnkey opportunity in a premier coastal destination. With decades of operating experience and deep community recognition, the company combines a high-traffic pier location with a full schedule of popular fishing excursions ranging from short bay and jetty trips to extended deep-sea adventures, appealing to both novice anglers and seasoned fishers alike. Guests enjoy professionally maintained vessels, modern safety equipment, amenities, and knowledgeable crew support, while the pier operations capture consistent daily foot traffic and ancillary revenue opportunities. Designed for scalability and with strong repeat customer demand, this business presents a rare lifestyle and investment opportunity in the recreational fishing and waterfront tourism market. VIEW BUSINESS SUMMARY

title: Established Relationship-Driven Commercial General Contractor
description: This well-established commercial general contracting firm, based in Colorado Springs, has been delivering exceptional service to clients throughout the Front Range for over two decades. Renowned for its commitment to high-quality craftsmanship, competitive pricing, and a hands-on approach, the company has built a strong reputation that fosters long-term client relationships and repeat business. Offering a comprehensive suite of services, the company supports projects from the initial pre-construction phase through final completion, tailoring its expertise to meet diverse project requirements. With a solid operational structure in place, the current owner has strategically positioned the company for continued success and is committed to ensuring a smooth transition for the new owner, with a flexible timeline for assistance. With 2025 revenue and profitability remaining strong, this firm continues to demonstrate its ability to thrive through challenging construction cycles making it an attractive acquisition for a construction-focused entrepreneur or industry buyer seeking expansion in Southern Colorado. DOWNLOAD BUSINESS SUMMARY

title: Process-Driven Construction & Exterior Trades Subcontractor
description: Denver-based construction subcontractor is a multi-trade provider recognized for its disciplined systems, long-tenured crews, and reliable support of leading general contractors. Founded in 2018 and strategically prepared for sale over the past three years, the business operates as a highly organized, process-driven firm with standardized SOPs, formalized workflows, and strengthened office operations that support consistent performance and scalability. Its flexible labor model—combining experienced 1099 crews with dedicated W-2 supervisors—enables broad trade coverage while maintaining strict quality control. The company’s agility allows it to pivot seamlessly between hail-related restoration, exterior siding and deck rebuilds, and specialized attic or confined-space work requiring advanced safety protocols. After a multi-year effort to optimize operations, the business is positioned for sale with mature systems, strong general contractor relationships, and a foundation built for growth. VIEW BUSINESS SUMMARY

title: Site Preparation & Civil Utility Contractor
description: This established Colorado civil construction and site-development company provides excavation, earthwork, underground utilities, demolition, hauling, concrete coring and sawing, erosion control, and related services throughout the Front Range. Its broad self-perform capabilities, experienced workforce, substantial equipment base, and established customer relationships provide strong control over project execution, scheduling, and costs. Following a temporary slowdown in Colorado new construction during 2025, market activity is trending upward as delayed projects move forward and development activity improves. With its strong reputation, diversified capabilities, and existing capacity, the Company represents an attractive acquisition platform for a strategic buyer seeking to expand its geographic reach, service offerings, and market presence as construction activity strengthens. VIEW BUSINESS SUMMARY

title: Versatile, Highly Reputable HVAC Services
description: This well-established heating and cooling business offers a strategic buyer an opportunity to expand its presence in the growing El Paso County market through an established brand, experienced workforce, loyal customer base, and hundreds of 5-star online reviews. Residential service and installation revenue has pivoted to approximately 70% of revenue, providing a strong foundation of recurring service, replacement, and new installation demand. While the residential construction slowdown created headwinds in 2025, 2026 activity has rebounded toward 2024 levels and continues to trend upward, positioning the business to benefit from improving construction activity and continued population growth. For an industry buyer, the company provides an attractive platform to increase market share, leverage operational synergies, expand service offerings, and accelerate growth without the time and expense required to build a comparable local presence organically. The real estate is also available for purchase, and ownership will provide transition support to facilitate a successful transition (time/length negotiable). BUSINESS SUMMARY LINK

title: High-Growth Spine & Regenerative Medicine Practice
description: This well-established outpatient specialty practice, located in a rapidly growing Colorado Front Range community, specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of spine, joint, and musculoskeletal conditions through a comprehensive range of non-surgical services. The practice has built an outstanding reputation for delivering personalized, patient-centered care while offering a balanced mix of insurance-based interventional procedures and cash-pay regenerative medicine treatments, as well as medical-legal services. Supported by experienced staff, efficient operational systems, stable revenues, and a loyal patient and referral base, the business is well-positioned for continued success. With continuing upward 2026 trends, strong market demand, and numerous opportunities to expand services, providers, and geographic reach, this represents an exceptional acquisition opportunity for a physician, healthcare organization, or strategic buyer seeking an established platform for future growth. VIEW BUSINESS SUMMARY

title: Established Heavy-Duty Truck Repair & Parts Business
description: Founded more than four decades ago, this well-established heavy-duty truck suspension and repair business has built an outstanding reputation for quality workmanship, technical expertise, and dependable customer service. Serving commercial fleets and owner-operators throughout Southern Colorado, the company provides comprehensive suspension, driveline, brake, steering, alignment, and other heavy-duty truck repair services from a fully equipped facility with oversized service bays and specialized equipment. Like many businesses across the industry, revenues have softened in recent years as freight activity normalized following the post-pandemic surge, fleets deferred discretionary maintenance amid higher operating costs and interest rates, and inflation increased labor and parts expenses. Despite these industry-wide headwinds, the business has maintained its loyal customer base, experienced workforce, and strong market reputation, creating an attractive opportunity for a new owner to capitalize on an established platform positioned to benefit as freight demand and fleet maintenance activity continue to strengthen over the long term. VIEW BUSINESS SUMMARY

title: Big Box Wholesale Importer/Distributor, RELOCATABLE
description: This tourism goods wholesale distributor, specializing in souvenirs, apparel, accessories, gifts, and more, has consistently demonstrated its growth trajectory year-over-year. The adept owners, skilled in marketing, have strategically positioned the company for ongoing expansion. The business offers diverse opportunities for its owners, whether engaging in travel across the Rocky Mountain region to connect with customers in independent and large retail outlets or adopting a semi-absentee ownership approach. With a reliable cash flow and impressive gross profit margins, the company stands out as a preferred supplier for many. Additionally, it benefits from access to an international design team and conducts operations in some of the most picturesque areas of the United States. This is an ideal acquisition for an entrepreneur who is ready to buy and scale a formidable business model. The owners are willing to fully train and help in the transition (time negotiable). Lender financing an option for a well-qualified buyer. Download Business Summary

title: Consistently Profitable Turf Installation Company
description: This company has grown tremendously and been profitable since year 1. It is primed for growth throughout Colorado and potentially into neighboring states. title: 692 BAYVIEW ROAD, MIDDLETOWN, DE, 19709
description:
A lovely brick federal style home with some Georgian characteristics. This home is placed on the national historic register. The property itself is 14.6 acres improved by mature trees, magnificent boxwoods, and lots of privacy. The home and numerous outbuildings were originally built during the local peach era, making Monterey one of Middletown's peach plantation homes. The outbuildings have just as much history as the main house.  
Additionally featured are several barns, a second 3 bedroom home, 4 car garage, and a 3 hole privy which is also on the historic register along with the unique ice and smoke houses.  
This country estate home is a great opportunity to add your restoration touches and make this your farmette in which to raise your kids, horses, and animals. 
No homesale contingencies

title: 30402 JAY PATCH ROAD, SELBYVILLE, DE, 19975
description: Welcome to the only USDA certified organic farm in Sussex County!  This 5.69 acre farm has everything you need to start farming this Spring 2026 including relationships with 4 local Farmers Markets and local restaurants.  DBA as Herb Spice Everything Nice for the past 20 years, the name is a well-known business in the Sussex County produce community.  The farm includes 2 greenhouses, 5 high tunnels, a 36 x 48 pole barn with an attached front porch and an attached 8 x 12 Vegetable Cooler/Propagation with 230 and 110 volt electric.  The field areas are protected with a 7.5 ft deer fence.  Included equipment is a 2008 Cub Cadet Tractor with a front load bucket and only 975 hours of use.  Compatible with the tractor includes a 60 inch tiller, 6 ft rear mower and a 30 inch bed layer with drip irrigation attachment.  See the Addendum for the full list of included equipment.  A 2016 Transit 250 truck fitted with shelving for produce delivery is negotiable.

title: 13651 WILSON HILL ROAD, GEORGETOWN, DE, 19947
description:
Three-house poultry farm in a strong Sussex County location with frontage on both Route 18 and Wilson Hill Road. Currently growing for Perdue, this property offers a solid opportunity for a buyer seeking existing poultry income, cropland value, and upside through approved improvements.

The poultry houses include a 44' x 460' house built in 1964, a 40' x 440' house built in 1974, and a 40' x 400' house built in 1984. House #2 recently experienced a fire and will require all new equipment, though the structure itself was not damaged. A replacement equipment quote from Marydel Ag is available at approximately $198,000. The farm is equipped with Chore-Time Model 40 controllers, Cyclone feeders in House #1, Chore-Time feeders in House #3, new nipples in both active houses, 3-year-old box heaters, three wells, and a 105 kW John Deere generator with approximately 1,200 hours. Electric service is provided by Delaware Electric Co-op.

Seller has already completed Perdue’s recent requirement for seven box heaters per house and $40,000 in foundation repairs on Houses 1 and 3. In addition, the farm has been approved through Energize Delaware for new doors, metal, plywood, and insulation to create solid side walls, plus ceiling re-insulation. The total quote is approximately $170,000, with 80% covered by Energize Delaware and the balance eligible for 3% financing. Seller is moving forward with the improvements but may also transfer the benefit of the approval to Buyer.

Nearly all remaining land is cleared tillable cropland, and the property offers highly favorable soils for a potential residential septic system, subject to Buyer’s own due diligence.

No showings inside the chicken houses unless birds are out.
